               Na, the head of accounting department (accountant in charge), have declared that they guarantee the truthfulness,
               accuracy and completeness of the financial statements contained in this annual report.

    V.         Profit distribution proposal or proposal for capitalisation of capital reserves of the Company for the Reporting Period
               considered and passed by the Board

               The Company intends to distribute a cash dividend of RMB1.35 (tax inclusive) for every 10 shares to all shareholders. Calculated
               based on the total share capital of 1,413,506,378 shares as at 31 December 2025, the total proposed cash dividends to be
               distributed amounts to RMB190,823,361.03 (tax inclusive). The total cash dividend of the Company for the Year (including cash
               dividend distributed for the interim period) amounts to RMB303,903,871.27 (tax inclusive), representing 30.14% of the net profit
               attributable to shareholders of the Company for the Year. The remaining undistributed profits of RMB1,655,047,324.36 will
               be carried forward for distribution in future periods. The Company did not convert capital reserve into share capital for 2025.
               If the total share capital of the Company changes before the record date for the implementation of dividend distribution, the
               Company shall maintain the distribution ratio per share unchanged and adjust the total distribution amount accordingly, and a
               separate announcement will be made to specify the adjustment.

               This profit distribution proposal is subject to approval at the 2025 annual general meeting of the Company. The Company
               expects to complete the payment of cash dividend on or before 16 July 2026.

                 Explanation on the major accounting information and financial indicators of the Company for the past three years as at the end
                 of the Reporting Period

                 1.      During the Reporting Period, focusing on its annual targets and tasks, seizing the opportunity presented by abundant
                         orders on hand and leveraging the advantages of series construction of its main vessel types, the Group continuously
                         deepened its lean management, strengthened full-process production control, and steadily increased its production
                         efficiency, achieving a cumulative operating revenue of RMB20,547 million, representing a year-on-year increase of
                         5.90%.

                 2.      During the Reporting Period, the Group achieved a cumulative net profit attributable to shareholders of the Company
                         of RMB1,008 million, representing a year-on-year increase of 167.26%; a net profit attributable to shareholders of the
                         Company after deduction of non-recurring gain or loss of RMB917 million, representing a year-on-year increase of
                         173.15%. It was mainly attributable to: (1) the further improvement of lean production and cost engineering, and the
                         year-on-year increase in the gross profit of products, as the Group continuously reduced the key cycles of main vessel
                         types, steadily improved production efficiency, and achieved results in refined management and cost control during the
                         Reporting Period; (2) the significant year-on-year increase in recognized investment income, as a result of the significant
                         improvement of operating results of the Company’s associates, and the increase in dividend amounts from its investee
                         companies during the Reporting Period.

                 3.      During the Reporting Period, the Group’s earnings per share was RMB0.7133, representing a year-on-year increase of
                         167.25%; and the earnings per share after deduction of non-recurring gains and losses was RMB0.6485, representing
                         a year-on-year increase of 173.17%; the weighted average return on equity was 5.76%, representing a year-on-year
                         increase of 3.56 percentage points; and the weighted average return on equity after deduction of non-recurring gains
                         and losses was 5.23%, representing a year-on-year increase of 3.27 percentage points.This was mainly due to the
                         impact of the increase in net income during the Reporting Period.

                 4.      During the Reporting Period, the net cash flows from operating activities of the Group amounted to RMB-0.322 billion
                         as compared to RMB-2.196 billion in the corresponding period last year, mainly due to the year-on-year increase in
                         milestone payments received for the construction of vessel products during the Reporting Period.

                 5.      At the end of the Reporting Period, the balance of exclusively state-owned capital reserve was RMB568 million, which
                         was mainly the state funds allocated to the infrastructure projects, which should be exclusively owned by the State as
                         capital investment by the State in the Company or subsidiaries after the completion and acceptance of the projects.
                         In accordance with relevant regulations such as the “Interim Measures for the Administration of the Restructuring and
                         Reorganization of Military Enterprises and Institutions and the Review of Military Operations on Capital Operations after
                         Listing” issued by the State Administration of Defense Science and Technology, the capital reserve formed by state-
                         allocated funds shall be owned by the representative of the investor of state-owned assets, i.e. CSSC, and shall be
                         converted into state-owned shares after fulfilling the necessary procedures in accordance with relevant regulations. The
                         impact of exclusively state-owned capital reserve was excluded when calculating the weighted average return on net
                         assets.

     SECTION III REPORT OF THE BOARD



     I.        BUSINESS ENGAGED IN BY THE COMPANY DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
               (i)     Principal activities

                       COMEC is engaged in its principal activities in three major sectors: defense industry, shipbuilding industry and emerging
                       industries, and its main products include defense equipment products including military ships, marine police equipment and
                       public service ships, shipbuilding and marine products including feeder containerships, bulk carriers, small and medium-sized
                       gas carriers, dredgers, offshore engineering platforms and wind power installation platforms, and emerging business products
                       represented by energy equipment and industrial internet platforms. During the Reporting Period, there was no material change
                       in the Group’s principal activities.

               (ii)    Business model

                       As a holding company, COMEC focuses on asset operation and investment management. Huangpu Wenchong, the holding
                       subsidiary of the Company, is engaged in manufacturing and providing customers with high-quality products through research and
                       development of ships, seeking orders and implementing customised order production, and have built up a modern shipbuilding
                       model highlighting general assembly process, refined management and information integration in the shipbuilding operation.
                       The Group is mainly engaged in assembly and construction in the shipbuilding and offshore engineering industrial chain. It has
                       extended to shipbuilding and offshore supporting products at the front end of the industrial chain and whole-life support at the
                       back end of the industrial chain.

               (iii)   Industry overview

                       The shipbuilding industry in which the Group operates is highly cyclical and is mainly subject to factors including the global
                       economic and trading trend, cyclical fluctuation in the shipping market and the international maritime conventions, and the
                       development and transformation of new technologies. For details of the shipbuilding industry during the Reporting Period,
                       please refer to part II of this section.

                       The Group is a large-scale backbone shipbuilding enterprise and a national core military production enterprise under China
                       Shipbuilding Group, its controlling subsidiary, Huangpu Wenchong, was founded in 1851, with a history of 175 years since its
                       establishment and 150 years of military production history, and its development history spans three centuries. It is the significant
                       construction base for military ships, special engineering ships and public service ships in China. It is also a world-leading
                       manufacturer of feeder containerships and the strongest dredging equipment manufacturing enterprise in Asia, and the largest
                       construction base for high-end maritime engineering equipment and offshore wind power infrastructure products in South China.

               (iv)    Analysis of factors driving change in business revenue

                       During the Reporting Period, the Group achieved an operating income of RMB20.547 billion, representing a year-on-year increase
                       of 5.90%, mainly due to the fact that the Group focused on its annual targets and tasks, seizing the opportunity presented by
                       abundant orders on hand, continuously deepening lean management, leveraging the advantages of series construction of its
                       main vessel types, strengthening production process control, and achieving sustained improvements in production efficiency
                       during the Reporting Period.

     II.       INDUSTRY IN WHICH THE COMPANY OPERATED DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
               (i)     Basic information on the shipbuilding industry

                       In 2025, impacted by the relatively sluggish global economy and disruptions from international political events, the market demand
                       in the global shipbuilding industry slowed down, the volume of new vessel transactions experienced a correction, and the price
                       of new vessels softened from their high levels. Nevertheless, the Chinese shipbuilding industry demonstrated strong resilience
                       and continued to maintain its global leading position.

                       The three major shipbuilding indicators recorded one decrease and two increases. In 2025, according to Clarkson’s
                       data statistics, the global new shipbuilding market received new orders for vessels of 151.9902 million DWT and 57.2825 million
                       CGT, representing a year-on-year decreases of 23.58% and 26.37%, respectively; shipbuilding completion volume stood at
                       97.3629 million DWT and 56.892 million CGT, representing a year-on-year increases of 8.82% and 6.07%, respectively; and the
                       orders on hand as at the end of the year was 447.7656 million DWT and 180.7358 million CGT, representing a year-on-year
                       increases of 21.67% and 14.73%, respectively. In 2025, due to the mismatch between high new vessel prices and relatively low
                       freight rates, compounded by factors such as the US Section 301 investigation into the maritime sector, frequent adjustments
                       to trade policies, tense global geopolitical landscapes, and uncertainties in technological pathways for green development, the
                       wait-and-see sentiment among shipowners intensified. Consequently, orders in the new shipbuilding market slowed down and
                       experienced a year-on-year decline, although it still remained at the second-highest level during the “14th Five-Year Plan” period.

                       Significant divergence was observed in the contracted volumes across specific vessel segments. In terms of major
                       vessel types, the contracted volume of containerships for the full year reached 54.234 million DWT, representing a year-on-year
                       increase of 4.8%; the contracted volumes of bulk carriers, oil tankers and liquefied gas carriers were 43.451 million DWT, 43.025
                       million DWT and 5.403 million DWT, representing a year-on-year decreases of 30.4%, 29.3% and 64.1%, respectively. As the
                       only vessel type to record growth, containerships remained highly active in 2025. The ordering demand for large containerships
                       from major liner companies remained robust, while the market’s attention to feeder containerships also increased significantly,
                       driving a strong release of new shipbuilding orders.

       The price of new vessels retreated slightly from their highs. In December 2025, the newbuilding price index closed at
       184.65 points, representing a decrease of 2.6% from the beginning of the year and a year-on-year decrease of 2.4%. By vessel
       type, the newbuilding price indices for containerships, bulk carriers, liquefied gas carriers and oil tankers in December closed at
       114.91 points, 168.33 points, 198.06 points and 213.21 points, respectively, representing a year-on-year decreases of 3.05%,
       3.46%, 4.34% and 4.43%, respectively. Currently, newbuilding prices have softened somewhat due to a contraction in transaction
       volumes. However, driven by positive factors on both the supply and demand sides, such as the scrapping of obsolete vessels,
       the release of renewal demand for green vessels, and the difficulty in significantly expanding premium shipbuilding capacity in
       the short term, abundant orderbooks and capacity bottlenecks continue to sustain prices at high levels.

       LNG remained the mainstream alternative marine fuel. In 2025, the global shipbuilding market continued to be guided
       by the overarching theme of green and low-carbon development, with newbuilding orders for alternative-fuel vessels for the
       full year reaching approximately 31.24 million CGT, accounting for 34.4% of the total newbuilding orders. Among which, LNG
       served as the primary alternative fuel and its share continued to increase, rising from 58.5% in 2024 to 83.7% in 2025, while
       methanol-fueled vessels accounted for 14.2%. By vessel type, the application of alternative fuels was relatively concentrated
       in containerships and LNG carriers, whereas its application in oil tankers and bulk carriers was relatively limited. Against the
       backdrop of uncertain technological pathways for marine fuels, a number of shipowners adopted “fuel-ready” designs, with
       methanol and ammonia emerging as the mainstream alternative options.

       China’s shipbuilding industry maintained its global leading position. In 2025, in the face of a complex international
       landscape and competition from Japan and South Korea, China’s shipbuilding industry withstood severe challenges and continued
       to consolidate its global leading position. According to data from the China Association of the National Shipbuilding Industry,
       in terms of DWT, China’s shipbuilding completions increased by 11.4% year-on-year, accounting for 56.1% of the global total;
       the volume of new orders received decreased by 4.6% year-on-year, accounting for 69.0%; and the volume of orders on hand
       increased by 31.5% year-on-year, accounting for 66.8%. The international market shares of these three major indicators have
       ranked first globally for 16 consecutive years. By vessel type, the market share of new orders for bulk carriers exceeded 80%
       for the first time, containerships secured approximately two-thirds of global orders, and oil tankers secured batch orders at
       year-end, thereby surpassing South Korea. Furthermore, gas carriers maintained an abundant orderbook and a stable market
       share, reflecting a continuous enhancement in comprehensive competitiveness.

       The offshore engineering market witnessed overall stable development. In 2025, newbuild demand in the global offshore
       engineering equipment market moderated somewhat, yet the overall performance remained above the average level over the
       past decade. For the full year, a total of 179 units of various types of offshore engineering equipment were contracted globally,
       representing a contract value of US$22.97 billion, a year-on-year decrease of 15.6%, while market prices for such equipment
       were sustained at high levels. China ranked first globally in terms of new orders received for offshore engineering equipment.
       In 2025, China secured orders for a cumulative total of 109 units of offshore engineering equipment with a contract value of
       US$7.45 billion, accounting for a global market share of 32.4% by contract value; South Korea and the United Arab Emirates
       ranked second and third with market shares of 19.6% and 16.0%, respectively.

(ii)   The development of industry-related policies and regulations

       In terms of international maritime rules and regulations, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) approved mid-term
       measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions at the MEPC83 meeting in 2025, launching the world’s first mandatory emission
       limitation and net-zero framework for greenhouse gas emissions covering the entire shipping industry, setting annual baseline
       targets for carbon intensity reduction and direct compliance targets, and imposing carbon emission fees on vessels exceeding
       the prescribed limit. In October of the same year, the IMO Special Committee decided to postpone the implementation of the
       net-zero framework for greenhouse gas emissions. The European Commission released the Clean Industrial Deal State Aid
       Framework (CISAF) in June 2025, providing a maximum subsidy of 45% for green hydrogen, ammonia and methanol projects
       (with an upper limit of 200 million euros for a single project), and requiring projects to use 100% renewable electricity, meet
       ISO14067 certification requirements for carbon footprint and prioritize supporting demonstration scenarios such as the Rotterdam-
       Singapore liquid ammonia fuel refueling route. The Council of the European Union officially implemented the Alternative Fuels
       Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) in 2025, specifying that TEN-T seaports shall be equipped with shore power facilities that comply
       with the IEC80005-1 standard for containerships and passenger ships by the end of 2029.

       In terms of China’s industrial policies, in 2025, a number of special supporting policies for the shipbuilding industry were
       introduced at the national level, which provide systematic guidance around the industry’s green and low-carbon transformation
       and response to external challenges. The Ministry of Transport issued relevant notices to further clarify the applicable requirements
       for scrap and renewal subsidy of old operating ships and to increase efforts in updating ship equipment, and in collaboration
       with multiple departments, issued guidance on the integrated development of transportation and energy and the high-quality
       development of inland waterway transportation, vigorously promoting the green and low-carbon substitution of ship power
       and the application of new and clean energy. The Maritime Safety Administration issued the “Interim Rules for Technology and
       Inspection of Methanol-fueled Ships (2025)” and the “Interim Rules for Technology and Inspection of Pure Battery-powered
       Ships (2025)”, improving relevant technical standard systems and ensuring the safe operation of new clean energy ships. The
       State Council revised the “Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on International Maritime Transportation”, authorizing
       corresponding countermeasures to be taken in response to international treaty disputes and foreign discriminatory measures; the
       Ministry of Transport issued the Announcement on the Collection of Special Port Service Fees from US-Related Vessels and its
       implementation measures, safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese industries and enterprises in accordance
       with the law and ensuring fair competition in international shipping.

       (Source: China Shipbuilding Group Economic Research Centre and China Association of the National Shipbuilding Industry, etc.)

     III.   OPERATION’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
            In 2025, the Company focused on its primary responsibilities and principal businesses, proactively addressed various complex changes
            and uncertainties, adhered to innovation-led development, and strengthened lean empowerment, thereby successfully accomplishing
            its annual tasks and the closing targets of the “14th Five-Year Plan”. Its value creation capability was continuously enhanced, and
            high-quality development was steadily advanced. The Company recorded an operating revenue of RMB20.547 billion, representing a
            year-on-year increase of 5.90%, and a net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company of RMB1.008 billion, representing a
            year-on-year increase of 167.26%.

            The Company deepened lean management, achieving steady improvements in operational quality and efficiency. In 2025,
            the Company focused on its annual targets and tasks, seized the development opportunities presented by an ample order book, and
            further advanced lean production and the enhancement of whole-process management. By optimising production processes, improving
            construction technologies, strengthening production planning, and promoting the synergy between cost engineering and resource
            allocation, the Company significantly shortened the critical construction cycles for its main ship types. This led to a simultaneous
            enhancement in shipbuilding efficiency, quality, and cost control, enabling the Company to accomplish its annual delivery targets ahead
            of schedule and achieve successive deliveries of key products. For the full year, a total of 39 vessels aggregating 1.1153 million DWT
            were delivered, encompassing key products such as defence equipment, feeder containerships, and scientific research vessels. The
            Company made remarkable progress in the construction of green vessels and smart vessels, successfully delivering the first batch of
            the 1250TEU methanol dual-fuel container ship series, the China’s first intelligent ocean-class research vessel “Tongji”, and the world’s
            first series of self-propelled enclosed salmon farming vessels; in the emerging industries segment, projects including the first large-scale
            overseas monopile project and the overseas wind power transition piece project were all delivered on schedule with high quality.

            The Company strengthened scientific and technological innovation and optimised its product portfolio. For the Year, the total
            value of new contracts secured amounted to RMB23.46 billion, representing 134% of the annual target. The Company secured orders
            for a total of 53 newbuild vessels across 10 types, including containerships, special ships, and gas carriers. The Company firmly fulfilled
            its primary responsibility of strengthening the armed forces, continued to deeply engage in the defence industry, enhanced its supply
            capability for new-quality and new-domain equipment, and proactively undertook equipment construction missions. In terms of civilian
            products, the Company accurately seized the structural opportunities in the global shipbuilding market. Driven by brand and technology,
            the Company focused on expanding the spectrum of its main ship types and promoted the continuous optimisation of its product mix.
            It maintained its leading position in the global feeder container ship market and successfully expanded into the market for 9200TEU
            large container ships, yielding remarkable results in product competitiveness and spectrum development. Concurrently, the Company
            vigorously advanced the development of its independently developed products. The “Honghu” series of container ships secured multiple
            batches of volume orders, and the order for the 5300TEU medium-sized container ship was successfully landed, marking the official
            expansion of its independently developed products from the feeder ship segment to the medium-sized container ship segment, thereby
            achieving a key breakthrough in its product line.

            As at the end of 2025, the Company held orders with the total contract value of approximately RMB60.6 billion, of which the total contract
            value of shipbuilding orders was approximately RMB59.1 billion, including 137 ship products and 2 offshore engineering equipment with
            a total of 4,527,400 DWT.

     IV.    ANALYSIS OF CORE COMPETITIVENESS DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
            (i)     Product advantages. The Group has mastered the capability of regional general assembly shipbuilding mode and simultaneous
                    construction of multiple vessel types, and it is in leading position in the technical indicators of military vessels, civil vessels and
                    offshore engineering business in China. The Group has developed a range of distinctive products for domestic and international
                    markets, including marine police equipment, public service equipment, feeder containerships, dredging vessels, etc. The Group
                    will continue to optimise and innovate ship models and enhance product performance, and extend its product lines based on
                    its existing strengths to form a diversified product portfolio to better meet customer needs.

            (ii)    Technological advantages. The Group has 13 science and technology innovation platforms at or above the provincial and
                    ministerial level, such as national enterprise technology center, postdoctoral research station, national engineering laboratory
                    for marine engineering R&D and design, Guangdong engineering technology research center, etc. It is one of the most capable
                    ship product development and design centers in South China and the first demonstration base of technological innovation for
                    military-civilian combination in Guangdong Province. The Group holds independent intellectual property rights in high technology
                    and high value-added products such as feeder containerships, public service ships, scientific exploration ships, wind power
                    installation platforms, high value-added products and special vessels. Adhering to an innovation-driven and technology-led
                    strategy, the Group tackled difficulties in cutting-edge technologies and focused on strengthening the research and development
                    of new green, energy-saving and environment-friendly ship types and high-tech and high value-added ship types.

            (iii)   Brand advantages. In the field of marine defense equipment, the Group is an important production and support facility for
                    military ships of the Chinese Navy in South China, and an important public service ship manufacturer in China. In the field of
                    shipbuilding and offshore engineering equipment, the Group has established a strong market reputation and holds a leading
                    position in the construction of multifunctional deep-sea survey ships, feeder containerships and dredging vessels. In the field
                    of emerging industries, the Group has a good reputation in the industry and has undertaken the construction of major steel
                    structures for national landmark infrastructure projects such as the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Channel and the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-
                    Macao Bridge, and its offshore wind power equipment has also entered into the international market.

            (iv)    Market advantages. The Group’s principal business and products have a high market share in domestic and overseas markets.
                    In particular, the Group holds a leading position globally in the markets for feeder containerships and dredgers and maintains
                    a leading position in the PRC in the markets for military ships, public service ships and dredgers.

            The above advantages have contributed to the sustainable development of the Group. In addition, amid the backdrop of green transformation
            and industry upgrading in the shipbuilding industry, the Group will focus on continuously strengthening its core competitiveness including
            research and development capability and building technologies, exploring new growth drivers, improving profitability and providing higher
            returns to shareholders.

                                 Description of principal business by industry, by product, by region and by sales model

                                 During the Reporting Period, the Group’s total income from its principal business amounted to RMB20.287
                                 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 5.84%, mainly due to the concentrated focus on its annual
                                 targets and tasks, seizing the opportunity presented by abundant orders on hand, continuously deepening lean
                                 management, leveraging the advantages of series construction of its main vessel types, strengthening production
                                 process control, and achieving sustained improvements in production efficiency during the Reporting Period.
                                 The gross profit of its principal business amounted to RMB2.021 billion, representing a year-on-year increase
                                 of RMB560 million, with gross profit margin at 9.96%, increasing 2.34 percentage points year-on-year, primarily
                                 contributed by the gross profit from the shipbuilding and steel structure engineering segments.

                                 In terms of product mix, the proportion of income from each segment showed year-on-year fluctuations during
                                 the Reporting Period, with a year-on-year increase in the proportion of income from shipbuilding, while proportion
                                 of income from offshore engineering products, ship repair and refit segments showed year-on-year decrease, and
                                 the proportion of income from other segments remaining largely flat compared with the last year. Among them,
                                 the proportion of income from shipbuilding products segments accounted for 91.06%, representing a year-on-
                                 year increase of 3.79 percentage points; the proportion of income from offshore engineering products accounted
                                 for 0.06%, representing a year-on-year decrease of 3.58 percentage points; the proportion of income from
                                 maintenance and modification on ships business accounted for 2.73%, representing a year-on-year decrease
                                 of 1.23 percentage points; the proportion of income from steel structure engineering business accounted for
                                 5.11%, and the proportion of income from electro-mechanical products and other business accounted for
                                 1.04%. During the Reporting Period, the income and gross profit of each business segment are as follows:

                                 1)      Shipbuilding business

                                         Income from the shipbuilding business was RMB18.472 billion, representing a year-on-year increase
                                         of 10.44%, and the gross profit margin was 10.27%, representing a year-on-year increase of 0.95
                                         percentage point. The increase in income and gross profit was mainly attributable to the sustained
                                         improvement in production efficiency driven by the advantages of abundant orders on hand and series
                                         construction of its main vessel types, as well as the effectiveness of cost control efforts under the
                                         deepening cost engineering initiative during the Reporting Period.

                                 2)      Offshore engineering business

                                         Income from the offshore engineering business was RMB13 million, representing a year-on-year
                                         decrease of 98.19%, and the gross profit margin was -332.72%, representing a year-on-year decrease
                                         of 311.72 percentage points. No new offshore engineering construction projects were commenced
                                         during the Reporting Period, and only incidental close-out and technical support work was carried out for
                                         offshore engineering products initiated in prior years. The construction technology and key performance
                                         requirements of such products are demanding, and the Group invested significant resources, resulting
                                         in a relatively high level of costs incurred.

                                 3)      Steel structure engineering business

                                         Income from steel structure engineering business was RMB1,038 million, representing a year-on-year
                                         increase of 25.55%, and the gross profit margin was 18.90%, representing a year-on-year increase of
                                         7.76 percentage points. The increase in income and gross profit was primarily due to the delivery of
                                         steel structure orders from overseas during the Reporting Period, with the delivered products carrying
                                         a relatively high gross margin, and the favourable US dollar settlement exchange rate.

                                 4)      Maintenance and modification on ships business

                                         Income from the maintenance and modification on ships business was RMB554 million, representing
                                         a year-on-year decrease of 26.93%, and the gross profit margin was -12.87%, representing a year-
                                         on-year decrease of 1.17 percentage points. The decrease in income and gross profit was primarily
                                         due to the fact that certain domestic ship maintenance projects had not yet been settled during the
                                         Reporting Period, and the final settlement prices for certain projects that were settled were lowered,
                                         resulting in negative gross margins for the relevant business.

       5)            Electro-mechanical products and other business

                     Income from electro-mechanical products and other business was RMB210 million, representing a

       By geographic region, during the Reporting Period, operating income from products sold to the PRC market
       (including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan) decreased by RMB1.497 billion year-on-year, representing a
       year-on-year decrease of 11.46%, and operating income from products sold to foreign markets increased by
       RMB2.617 billion year-on-year, representing a year-on-year increase of 42.86%, mainly due to the differences
       in the geographical distribution of customers for the orders on hand during the Reporting Period. The gross
       profit margin of products sold to the PRC (including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan) was 6.06%, with the
       gross profit level basically flat as compared with that of the previous year. The gross profit margin of products
       sold to foreign markets was 15.13%, representing a year-on-year increase of 4.89 percentage points, mainly
       because the majority of exported vessel products delivered during the Reporting Period were primarily series
       ships, which facilitated cost control and resulted in a favourable gross profit situation.

                                 1)             During the Reporting Period, impairment losses in shipbuilding products business segment amounted
                                                to RMB-28 million, compared with RMB25 million in the corresponding period of the previous year,
                                                mainly due to the impact of reversal of impairment provision for products completed for sale during
                                                the Reporting Period.

                                 2)             During the Reporting Period, the direct material and processing costs of the offshore engineering
                                                products business segment decreased by 97.43% and 84.17% year-on-year respectively, which
                                                was mainly attributable to the fact that there was no new offshore engineering products construction
                                                business during the Reporting Period, leading to a significant decrease in overall investment compared
                                                to the previous year.

                                 3)             During the Reporting Period, direct materials of the steel structure engineering business segment
                                                increased by 40.33% year-on-year, which was mainly due to the relatively high proportion of materials
                                                used in overseas steel structure projects delivered during the Reporting Period.

                                 4)             During the Reporting Period, the processing costs for the maintenance and modification on ships
                                                business segment decreased by 36.03% year-on-year, mainly due to the difference in project structure
                                                as the proportion of processing fees for overseas ship maintenance settled during the Reporting Period
                                                was relatively low.

                                 5)             During the Reporting Period, direct materials and the processing costs for the electromechanical
                                                products and other business segments increased by 64.44% and 34.37% year-on-year respectively,
                                                which was mainly due to the year-on-year increase in revenue during this Reporting Period, which led
                                                to a corresponding increase in cost investments.

(3).   Explanation

       In 2025, the Group adhered to the innovation-driven development, continued to improve and optimise the
       mechanism of scientific and technological innovation, and actively promoted the construction of innovation
       capability, resulting in a continuous improvement in its technological level. Firstly, the Group completed the
       design and upgrading of several types of independently developed products. Throughout the year, the Group
       carried out design and development tasks for a range of independently developed and upgraded products,
       forming a series of proprietary ship design solutions covering container ships, gas carriers, bulk carriers and other
       sectors, thereby significantly enhancing the design product pipeline and market responsiveness. Secondly, the
       Group enhanced research into smart manufacturing and advanced processes, focusing on the research and
       application of advanced technologies such as digital machining of internal components, small-part polishing,
       robotic welding for assembly, centralised control systems for sheet metal cutting, and digital handover systems
       for pallets, with a view to significantly improving production and construction efficiency. Thirdly, the Group
       strengthened scientific research management. The Company completed 375 patent applications, including
       370 invention patents, and obtained 216 patent grants for the year, which has continuously strengthened its
       technological reserves.

     have considered and approved the “Proposal on Conducting Foreign Exchange Derivatives Trading in 2025”, agreeing
     that the Company and its subsidiaries shall conduct foreign exchange derivative trading business, with a balance of

     of COMEC on Resolutions of the 2024 Annual General Meeting” published by the Company on the website of the
     SSE (www.sse.com.cn) and the website of the Stock Exchange (www.hkexnews.hk) dated 28 March 2025 and 27

                                           2.       Risk management measures (1) The objective of entering into foreign
                                                    exchange derivatives trading is to mitigate the impact of foreign
                                                    exchange fluctuation on the Company. Financial derivatives with
                                                    simple structure, high liquidity and identifiable risks shall be selected
                                                    to conduct hedging business, and any speculative activities are
                                                    prohibited. The amount of foreign exchange derivatives trading shall
                                                    not exceed the authorised limit approved by the Company. (2) The
                                                    Company has formulated the Management Measures for Financial
                                                    Derivative Activities, which establishes clear regulations on operation
                                                    principles, authority for approval, management and internal operation
                                                    procedures, internal risk reporting system and risk handling procedures
                                                    of foreign exchange derivatives trading activities. (3) Counterparty
                                                    management is strengthened. Only those foreign exchange derivatives
                                                    that are closely related to the Company’s principal business shall be
                                                    selected, and the derivatives shall be matched with the business in
                                                    terms of the types, scales, directions and durations. The Company
                                                    shall enter into contracts with clear terms with the counterparties and
                                                    strictly implement the risk management system so as to prevent legal
                                                    risks. (4) The finance department of the Company shall be responsible
                                                    for monitoring the changes in the open market price or the fair value
                                                    of the derivatives, and assessing the changes in the risk exposure
                                                    of the invested derivatives on a timely basis. It shall promptly report
                                                    any major changes in the market or significant unrealised losses to
                                                    the Company’s management and the Board, which shall establish
                                                    an emergency mechanism to actively respond and properly deal with
                                                    the situation. (5) The audit department of the Company, acting as the
                                                    supervision department of the Company’s financial derivatives trading,
                                                    shall be responsible for supervising and inspecting the compliance
                                                    of the decision-making, management and execution of the financial
                                                    derivatives trading of the Company.

VI.   DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF THE COMPANY CONCERNING THE FUTURE
      DEVELOPMENT OF THE COMPANY
      (I)     Industry landscape and trends

              The defense industry is navigating a period of a strategic opportunity window. Against the backdrop of continued
              tensions in the global geopolitical situation and prolonged geopolitical conflicts, there persists an enduring necessity to strengthen
              the nation’s defense capabilities. Achieving the centennial goal of military establishment by 2027 as scheduled is a key node in
              the process of advancing the modernisation of national defense and the military. The subversive role of emerging technologies
              has put forward new requirements for the PRC’s defense and military manufacturing industry, such as “new domain and new
              quality”, “intelligence”, “combat-oriented military training” and “border, maritime and air defense construction”, leading the
              subsequent development direction of defense and military enterprises. The deep integration of artificial intelligence, big data, and
              new materials technology with the shipbuilding industry is reshaping the form and capabilities of law enforcement equipment.

              The shipbuilding industry as a whole remained highly prosperous. The global shipbuilding industry is currently at a critical
              development stage characterised by the superposition of the “dual cycles” of the renewal of aging vessels and the green and
              low-carbon transformation of fleets. In terms of demand for vessel renewal, as of the end of December 2025, the size of global
              shipping capacity with a vessel age of 20 years and above reached 450 million DWT, which was substantially on par with the
              size of the order book held by global shipyards; the shipping capacity with a vessel age of 15 to 19 years exceeded 550 million
              DWT,it is expected that the phase‑out will be progressively completed over the next decade, generating substantial demand for
              fleet renewal within the industry. In terms of demand for incremental capacity, maritime trade is set to slow to an annual growth
              rate of 1 to 2% amid subdued global economic expansion. Nevertheless, adjustments in the pattern of international trade and
              persistently low fleet operating efficiency are still expected to support a steady rise in maritime throughput, providing effective
              underpinning for additional capacity. At the same time, under the influence of factors such as weak global economic recovery,
              trade policy volatility, an uncertain pathway for green, low‑carbon technologies, as well as wide swings in freight rates and high
              newbuilding prices, the market is exposed to short term cyclical adjustment pressure. In 2026, global shipbuilding capacity is
              likely to remain tight, shipyards’ orderbooks will stay full, and the industry is expected to exhibit a “stable volume, high price”
              profile overall, presenting a mix of opportunities and challenges.

              Emerging industries are showing a clear incremental growth trajectory. According to the Global Wind Energy Council
              (GWEC), the global offshore wind power industry is projected to continue expanding, with a CAGR in new installations worldwide
              of around 20.6% between 2025 and 2030. Driven by nearshore resource saturation, policy incentives steering development further
              offshore, and the maturation of large scale turbines and floating technology, the focus of offshore wind power development will
              shift towards deeper waters and more distant sites.

              (Source of relevant data: China Shipbuilding Group Economic Research Centre, etc.)

      (II)    The Company’s development strategy

              With the aim of strengthening the military, serving the nation, and deepening the cultivation in the marine sector, the Group
              is committed to building high-quality marine equipment and aims to become a world-class listed marine defense equipment
              company with a rational industrial structure, leading core technologies, excellent quality and services and strong international
              competitiveness.

              Facing the new development landscape of the shipbuilding market, the Company adheres to the enterprise spirit of “innovation,
              efficiency, cooperation and win-win”, follows the development concept of “devoting to both manufacturing and service”, and
              actively builds up three major industrial layouts of marine defense equipment, ship and offshore engineering equipment and
              marine science and technology innovation equipment. The Company fully aligns with major strategies such as the “Belt and
              Road” Initiative, military-civilian integration development, the building of a strong manufacturing country and the building of a
              strong maritime country, while promoting the expansion and extension of the traditional manufacturing industry in a more valuable
              direction, strengthening and optimising the main business, vigorously expanding emerging industries, driving transformation and
              upgrading into advanced manufacturing and service industries, and achieving high-quality development.

      (III)   Business plan

              In 2025, the Group recorded an operating income of RMB20.547 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of 5.90%; and
              secured orders with contract value of RMB23.455 billion, which was 134.41% of the annual target.

              In 2026, the Group plans to realise operating income of RMB21.218 billion and to secure orders with contract value of RMB16.424
              billion. The Group will focus on its main ship types, strengthen the development of independently developed ship types and
              spectrum expansion, consolidate its market share in the medium-sized container ship market, step up efforts in market expansion,
              persist in leading the market with brand and technology, and enhance its core market competitiveness; improve the production
              and technical preparation system, deepen the production management and control mechanism, and optimise the construction
              paths, key cycles and supporting capabilities for main ship types to drive the improvement of production efficiency; deepen
              the efficacy of digital and intelligent leadership, improve the establishment of a lean management system, further advance cost
              management and control, and enhance its value creation capability. Through the above measures, the Group will ensure the
              implementation of the 2026 business plan.

              The aforementioned business plan does not constitute a performance commitment by the Company to investors. Investors are
              advised to pay attention to investment risks.

          (iv)    Potential Risks

                  1.      Macro‑market risk: The industry faces rising uncertainties. Significant shifts in the external environment, such as
                          regional protectionism, geopolitical conflict, or policy changes in countries affecting China’s shipbuilding sector, could
                          dampen international shipping and fleet renewal demand, intensify market competition, and place pressure on the
                          Company’s market expansion and order intake. The Group will continuously monitor industry trends and changes in
                          external environment, proactively respond to market and policy adjustments, pursue innovation‑led growth, increase
                          investment in green ship R&D, and steadily enhance its core competitiveness.

                  2.      Construction‑schedule risk: As the shipbuilding industry is currently in an upcycle, the Company has a sufficient
                          backlog of orders on hand and full production commitments. External factors, including geopolitical developments, create
                          uncertainties in the supply chain and procurement security, resulting in the risk of delayed supply of key equipment
                          and materials. At the same time, a higher proportion of technologically sophisticated vessels increases construction
                          complexity and heightens safety and quality management requirements, challenging project schedule control. The Group
                          will strengthen supply‑chain coordination and procurement management, secure critical resources in advance, optimise
                          production organisation and technical applications, enforce strict safety and quality controls, with a view to ensuring
                          orderly construction progress.

                  3.      Customer Performance Risk: As a result of changes in the global economy, geopolitics, and shipping trade, ship
                          owners may experience difficulties in financing and tight funds, resulting in default in shipbuilding payment, deferred
                          recognition of delivery, amendment of contracts or even abandonment of ships, which will subject the Company’s
                          orders on hand to default risk. The Group will further strengthen the management of contract performance, enhance
                          the creditworthiness investigation of ship owners and project process management, improve the risk early warning
                          mechanism, and ensure the smooth delivery of orders on hand.

                  4.      Cost Control Risk: Given the Group’s order-based production and long construction cycle for shipbuilding business,
                          and fluctuations in the prices of raw materials such as steel coupled with the increase in labour costs, may lead to a
                          passive increase in the costs of the Company’s products under construction, which will have a certain impact on the
                          Company’s operating results. The Group will continue to improve efficiency and reduce costs across the entire industrial
                          chain and optimise the product structure by promoting the mass production of main construction products and increasing
                          the proportion of high value-added products to minimise the impact of cost fluctuations on the Company.

                  5.      Exchange-rate volatility risk: The Group’s exchange rate risk arises from the possibility of the increase or decrease
                          in the value of assets (or creditor’s rights) and liabilities (or debts) denominated in foreign currencies due to exchange
                          rate fluctuations. It is mainly concentrated on export shipbuilding orders denominated in United States dollars. The
                          Group will continue to adhere to the aim of risk prevention, base its approach on the exchange rates applicable to its
                          operating orders, strengthen the analysis of exchange rate trend and formulate exchange rate risk prevention plans by
                          using financial tools such as forward exchange contracts and options to protect against exchange rate risk.

     I.       INFORMATION ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
              (I)     Corporate culture, mission and objectives

                      Corporate Culture

                      The core of our corporate culture is “innovation, efficiency, cooperation and win-win”, among which, “innovation” means the
                      Company insists on innovation-driven development focusing on key tasks, and constantly creates a new situation; “efficiency”
                      means the Company achieves the goal of high quality and high efficiency through the unity and collaboration of all the employees
                      and innovative development; “collaboration” means all employees of the Company collaborate to form a resultant force around
                      the Company’s strategic positioning and based on their positions; and “win-win” means insisting on people-oriented, sharing
                      development achievements to achieve the common growth of employees and the Company.

                      Corporate mission

                      The corporate mission of the Company is to fulfill the duty of strengthening the military and serving the nation, support the
                      construction of a maritime power, and drive the value creation as a central enterprise.

                      The Company fulfills the duty of strengthening the military and serving the nation by making the development of the military
                      equipment and the military industry as a major political responsibility and the primary mission, and provides impetus and guarantee
                      for the construction of a first-class military central enterprise group by making full use of the Company’s capital market status
                      as a listed company in Shanghai and Hong Kong.

                      The Company supports the construction of a maritime power by giving full play to its role and advantages as an A+H listed
                      central enterprise, and vigorously promotes the progress of the construction of a maritime power by relying on national regional
                      strategies such as the construction of Guangdong, Hong Kong, Macao and the Greater Bay Area.

                      The Company is committed to achieving the value creation as a central enterprise, continues to strengthen its core competitiveness,
                      mainly provides capital and innovation strength for the development of the Group, serves the Group’s high-quality development
                      with dual drivers, and promote the value creation of central enterprises.

                      Strategic objectives

                      The strategic objectives of the Company are to build high-quality marine equipment, strengthen the military and serve the nation,
                      and become a world-class listed marine equipment company with reasonable industrial structure, leading core technology,
                      excellent quality and service and strong international competitiveness by focusing on the marine industry and developing
                      harmoniously.

                      Adhering to the development philosophy of “innovation, coordination, green, openness and sharing”, the Company actively
                      responds to the Group’s high quality development strategy, constructs scientific and reasonable industrial layouts, fully aligns
                      with major strategies such as “Belt and Road”, military-civilian integration development for the building of a strong manufacturing
                      country and a strong maritime country, focusing on “optimizing structure, deepening reform, capital-driven and innovative
                      development”, promoting the expansion and extension of the traditional manufacturing industry in a direction towards higher
                      value, so as to strengthen and optimize its main business, vigorously expand emerging industries, accelerate the Company’s
                      transformation and upgrading, and achieve high-quality development.

              (II)    Corporate governance

                      The Company always strictly conforms to the Company Law of the PRC, the Securities Law of the PRC, relevant regulations
                      issued by the CSRC and the listing rules of the SSE and the Stock Exchange by continuously improving its corporate governance
                      structure and standardizing its operations. During the Reporting Period, the Company’s governance had no material deviations
                      from the Company Law and relevant regulations issued by the CSRC. The Company has adopted the Corporate Governance
                      Code and Corporate Governance Report(“Corporate Governance Code”) as set out in Appendix C1 to the Stock Exchange

                      Company has been in strict compliance with the principles of good corporate governance, the code provisions on a “comply

                  Diversity of Board members

                  In accordance with the requirements of the Listing Rules of the Stock Exchange, the Board has formulated and adopted the
                  Board Diversity Policy. This policy emphasizes that the Company will, when determining the composition of the Board members,
                  consider the diversity of Board members from various aspects. All appointments of the Board shall be based on the principle
                  of meritocracy, and candidates will be considered based on objective conditions, having due regard for the benefits of diversity
                  of Board members, as well as factors including gender, age, cultural and educational background, professional experience,
                  skills, knowledge and service tenure. The Company will consider its own business model and specific needs from time to time,
                  and ultimately make decisions based on the strengths of the candidates and the contributions they can make to the Board.

                  Pursuant to the abovementioned policy, the Nomination Committee has reviewed the composition of the Board and management
                  members of the Company in accordance with the requirements of the Listing Rules, taking into account:

                  •        Age: Currently, the members of the Board and senior management cover a wide range of age groups, and the diversity
                           in age groups helps to bring diversified thinking to Board members;

                  •        Education background and professional knowledge: Board members come from different educational backgrounds,
                           covering professions such as ship engineering, water transportation engineering, precision instrument, physics, business
                           administration, international finance, economics, accounting and law. All Directors have obtained master’s and doctoral
                           degrees, professor’s qualifications and other professional recognition qualifications, including researcher-level senior
                           engineer, researcher-level senior accountant, senior economist, senior certificated accountant in Australia, American
                           Certified Management Accountant, senior accountant, senior management accountant, etc. This also reflects that the
                           marine defense equipment industry, ship and offshore engineering equipment Industry, marine science and technology
                           innovation and application industry and other businesses of the Group involve various different professional fields. The
                           educational backgrounds of Board members help to ensure the professionalism of the Group’s businesses; and

                  •        Industry experience: Board members have relatively sufficient industry experience in their respective fields, including
                           involvement in various domestic businesses in terms of project operations such as ship engineering, defense equipment
                           configuration, heavy industry, financial management and others, bringing foresight to the Company’s business development
                           as well as on a macro perspective.

                  As at the date of the Report, the Board of the Company has one female member, which was introduced by the Company to

                  diversity goal set by the Company has been achieved.

           The Group is committed to creating a diversified and inclusive corporate culture, establishing a fair and just employment
           mechanism, continuously improving a scientific talent retention, promotion and development system, designing compensation,
           benefits and care policies that run through the full life cycle of employees’ career, comprehensively ensuring the career
           development and workplace experience of employees, and enhancing their sense of happiness and belonging. During the
           Reporting Period, the Company followed the principles of “openness, equality, competition and meritocracy” to publicly recruit
           and cultivate employees. As at the end of the Reporting Period, the Group had a total of 4,462 employees, of which 634 were
           female employees, accounting for 14.20% of all employees, which was due to the fact that the Group actively built up three
           major industrial layouts of “marine defense equipment industry”, “ship and offshore engineering equipment Industry” and “marine
           science and technology innovation and application industry”, and the Group’s businesses mainly focused on shipbuilding and
           offshore engineering manufacturing, which laid a relatively high demand for employees’ labour and physical strength, resulting
           in more male employees responsible for certain types of works in the actual implementation of work. Among all employees, 666
           (accounting for approximately 14.93% of all employees) fell within the age group of under 30 years old, while 3,222 (accounting
           for approximately 72.21% of all employees) fell within the age group of 30 to 50 years old. This precisely reflected the Group’s
           active inclusion of young talents and the cultivation of suitable talents in all age groups, providing promotion opportunities, and
           striving to continuously improve the diversity of employees, senior management and Directors of the Group in terms of personal
           abilities, professional backgrounds and gender. At the same time, the Group upheld the philosophy of inclusive talent, promoted
           workplace inclusion, created a diversified and high-quality talent echelon and built a career platform with equality. The Company
           treated employees fairly and equally. The Company paid attention to promoting employment for local residents, women, ethnic
           minorities and college students, and strove to increase employment opportunities in local communities. The Company publicly
           recruited from society without setting restrictions on race, gender, religious beliefs and other conditions. Based on the above,
           the Company believed that the diversity among employees had been achieved and it was committed to gradually enhancing
           the diversity of gender, age group, educational and professional background in future Board re-election and staff training and
           promotion.

                  –       Formulating, considering and reviewing the Company’s corporate governance policy, principle, convention, practice and

                  –       Developing, examining and monitoring the code of conduct and compliance manual (if any) applicable to employees
                          and Directors;

                          limited to the new CG Code, as well as the requirements of the CSRC on corporate governance, and the Company’s

                  The Board endeavors to maintain on-going communication with shareholders and considers general meetings as a major
                  opportunity to keep contact with shareholders. All shareholders holding shares of the Company are entitled to attend general

                  extraordinary general meeting at least ten business days (being the day on which trading of securities commences on the Stock
                  Exchange) or fifteen days (whichever is longer) prior to the extraordinary general meeting, and publish an announcement and
                  distribute a circular in accordance with the relevant rules, setting out in detail the matters to be considered at the meeting and
                  the procedures for voting thereat. Separate resolutions are proposed at the general meeting and voted on by way of poll on
                  each separate issue, including the election of individual Directors. The voting method and procedures at general meetings are

                  shareholders’ circular and explained at the meeting. For information of Directors’ attendance at general meetings, please refer

           of the Group, industry prospects, and financing plans on a regular basis. Subject to compliance with applicable laws
           and regulations, the Company will strengthen communication with all parties in accordance with the methods formulated
           in the aforementioned Investor Relations Management Policy. In order to enhance the transparency of information
           disclosure of the Company, the Company will continue, subject to compliance with relevant laws and regulations,
           to provide relevant information on a regular basis and as and when appropriate. In summary, based on the multiple
           existing communication channels with shareholders and investors and their feedbacks, the Company believes that its
           communication policy with investors has been effectively implemented during the Reporting Period.

           The Board is grateful to shareholders and other stakeholders for their continued support to the Group and welcomes
           their views as well as any inquiries they may have about the management and governance of the Company.

      3.   Shareholders’ Rights

           Ways for shareholders to convene extraordinary general meeting

           Shareholders separately or aggregately holding over 10% of shares of the Company shall be entitled to request and
           demand the Board to convene extraordinary general meetings and shall make written request to the Board. The Board
           shall reply in writing regarding the acceptance or refusal to convene the extraordinary general meeting within 10 days
           upon receiving the request in accordance with the requirements of the laws, administrative regulations and the Articles
           of Association.

           If the Board agrees to convene the extraordinary general meeting, notice convening the meeting shall be issued within
           5 days upon making the Board resolutions. Should there be amendments to the original requests in the notice, consent
           has to be obtained from the relevant shareholders. If the Board does not agree to convene the extraordinary general
           meeting or does not reply within 10 days upon receiving the request, shareholders separately or aggregately holding
           over 10% of shares of the Company shall be entitled to request the Audit Committee to convene the extraordinary
           general meeting, and shall make request to the Audit Committee in writing.

           If the Audit Committee agrees to convene the extraordinary general meeting, notice convening the meeting shall be
           issued within 5 days upon receiving the request. Should there be amendments to the original requests in the notice,
           consent has to be obtained from the relevant shareholders. If the Audit Committee fails to issue a notice of the general
           meeting within a specified period, it shall be deemed that the Audit Committee shall not convene and preside over the
           general meeting, the shareholder(s) separately or aggregately holding above 10% of the shares of the Company for 90
           consecutive days or more may convene and preside over the meeting by himself/herself/themselves.

           Shareholder(s), if decided to convene general meetings on their own, shall inform the Board in writing and make filing
           with the stock exchange for record.

           The Company will bear all the necessary costs for the general meeting convened by the shareholder(s).

                          Procedures for shareholders to raise inquiry to the Board and related information

                          The shareholders of the Company shall be entitled to the right to inspect and make copy of the Articles of Association,

                          Company, he shall submit a written request to the Company stating the purpose. Shareholders may entrust intermediary
                          organisations such as an accounting firm, a law firm or other intermediary to inspect the materials specified in the
                          preceding paragraph. The shareholder and the engaged accounting firm, law firm or other intermediary shall comply
                          with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations relating to the protection of state secrets, commercial secrets,
                          personal privacy and personal information when they inspect the materials and make copy thereof.

                          Shareholder(s) request to inspect the aforesaid information or obtain material shall submit their inquiries through the
                          Company’s address in domestic (No. 10, Jibaosha North Road, Nansha District, Guangzhou) or Hong Kong (17/F, Far
                          East Finance Centre, 16 Harcourt Road, Hong Kong), and provide the Company with written documents evidencing
                          the class and number of shares of the Company held by them. After checking and verifying shareholders’ identity, the
                          Company will provide related information or documents.

                          Procedures for putting forward proposals at general meeting

                          Shareholders separately or collectively holding more than 1% of the shares of the Company, may propose extraordinary
                          motions to the convener in writing within 10 days before the convening of such general meeting. The convener shall
                          issue supplementary notice of the general meeting to announce the content of the extraordinary motions within 2 days
                          after receiving the proposed motions.

                  4.      The Company’s Independence from the Controlling Shareholder

                          During the Reporting Period, the controlling shareholder of the Company had never been involved in any acts of
                          bypassing the general meeting or interfering, whether directly or indirectly, with the Company’s decision-making or
                          operation. The Company and China Shipbuilding Group are independent of each other in terms of personnel, assets,
                          finance, organization and business.

                          The connected transactions between the Company and CSSC were carried out in strict compliance with the listing
                          rules of the relevant stock exchanges in Shanghai and Hong Kong with the prior approval of independent non-executive
                          Directors and were reviewed by the Audit Committee. For material connected transactions, independent financial advisors
                          had been appointed to express their opinions. It is the policy of the Company and China Shipbuilding Group to conduct
                          monthly monitoring of continuing connected transactions and report to the Board on a monthly basis and to Directors
                          on the safety of connected deposits on an annual basis. During the Reporting Period, the total value of continuing
                          connected transactions did not exceed the annual caps approved at the shareholders’ meeting.

                          Controlling shareholder, actual controller and other units under its control engaged in business which is the same as or
                          similar to the Company’s business, impact on the Company of horizontal competition or significant change in horizontal
                          competition, and resolving measures taken, its progress and follow-up plans

                          On 24 January 2025, the Company received the “Letter on the Request to Revise the Content of Letter of Undertaking
